findings.summary: tools/env.sh normalizes PATH with an explicit colon-remainder loop instead of implicit word splitting, which ordinary zsh does not perform. Exact duplicates of the selected Node directory and ~/.local/bin are removed wherever they sit and the order [selected Node >=22][~/.local/bin][rest] is pinned, identically on first and repeated activation in bash and zsh; unrelated entries and paths containing spaces are preserved and no IFS, glob or shell option and no global config are changed. Verified by: the validator-owned launcher_shell_contract.py (PASS in bash and zsh, identical PATH over two activations, spaced directory preserved); the original launcher_contract.py (both scenarios PASS); a live path-stability probe on the laptop showing node-dir and user-bin exactly once on both activations in both shells; the labelled fresh-terminal and controlled cases; and spec/import/combat/Guard runs through the route. The earlier defect (zsh received the whole PATH as one segment, so duplicates accumulated) is fixed; the system python3.8 venv limitation is unchanged.
